title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters
text: id: COMP-009 domain: math title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters tags: ratio, mixture, parts memory: A mixture ratio felt like two numbers competing until I counted total parts. Two parts and five parts made seven parts total, and I wrote total volume divided by total parts to find liters per part. Only then did I multiply by each side of the ratio. The concentrate and water added back to the requested total.

title: Ratio Unit Part Was Written Before Both Amounts
text: id: COMP-023 domain: math title: Ratio Unit Part Was Written Before Both Amounts tags: ratio, mixture, unit-part, correction memory: I once solved a ratio mix and skipped the unit-part line, which made the work hard to audit. The clean version wrote the parts first, then total divided by total parts: 2 plus 5 equals 7 parts, and 42 divided by 7 equals 6 liters per part. Then 2 parts became 12 liters concentrate and 5 parts became 30 liters water.
